numerical_failure.affected_api: pandas._libs.src.vendored.numpy.datetime.np_datetime.c (C function converting pandas datetime structs to int64 nanoseconds; scaleMicrosecondsToNanoseconds is the overflowing helper)
numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Timestamps near the minimum representable value raise OverflowError because scaleMicrosecondsToNanoseconds overflows as an intermediate step when scaling microseconds to nanoseconds, even though adding back the nanoseconds part would bring the value back into int64 range. For example, microseconds -9223372036854776 scales to -9223372036854776000, which is below INT64_MIN (-9223372036854775808).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Timestamps such as 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224193 through 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224999 should be valid and not raise OverflowError; the final nanosecond value should be computed without overflowing the intermediate scaled microseconds.
trigger_conditions: timestamp near the lower int64 nanosecond bound, e.g. 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224193 through 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224999
base is NPY_FR_ns and microseconds equals min_nanoseconds / 1000 - 1
intermediate scaling of microseconds to nanoseconds overflows before the sub-microsecond part (dts->ps / 1000) is added back
adding a whole microsecond to the timestamp does not trigger the problem

category_specific_evidence: Violated property: the intermediate scaling of microseconds to nanoseconds overflows int64 for near-minimum timestamps, while adding back the nanoseconds part (dts->ps / 1000) brings the result back into the valid range; the fix computes NPY_MIN_INT64+1 plus (dts->ps - _NS_MIN_DTS.ps)/1000 directly when microseconds == min_nanoseconds/1000 - 1
Concrete values: timestamps 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224193 through 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224999 previously raised OverflowError; 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145225000 always worked
Issue #57150: pd.Series([pd.Timestamp.min.tz_localize('utc')]).dtype changes to object in pandas 2.2.0, while it stays datetime64[ns, UTC] in 2.1.4; expected behavior is to keep datetime64[ns, UTC]

provenance.value: pandas._libs.src.vendored.numpy.datetime.np_datetime.c (C function converting pandas datetime structs to int64 nanoseconds; scaleMicrosecondsToNanoseconds is the overflowing helper)

Timestamps near the minimum representable value raise OverflowError because scaleMicrosecondsToNanoseconds overflows as an intermediate step when scaling microseconds to nanoseconds, even though adding back the nanoseconds part would bring the value back into int64 range. For example, microseconds -9223372036854776 scales to -9223372036854776000, which is below INT64_MIN (-9223372036854775808).

Timestamps such as 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224193 through 1677-09-21 00:12:43.145224999 should be valid and not raise OverflowError; the final nanosecond value should be computed without overflowing the intermediate scaled microseconds.
